text: In Papua New Guinea, Papua New Guineans are known for speaking over 800 diverse languages, reflecting a high linguistic density and cultural diversity. This behavior serves the goal of communicating and showcasing the remarkable diversity present within the country. Papua New Guinea is recognized as the most culturally diverse country globally, with over 800 living languages and 5 ethnic groups, highlighting the rich tapestry of traditions and languages. This practice of speaking numerous languages and embracing cultural diversity is widely regarded as a normative and standard behavior among the sampled population, reflecting the deep-rooted value placed on linguistic and cultural variety within Papua New Guinean society.

In Papua New Guinea, people and tribes engage in behaviors focused on adaptation, nurturing, and maintaining their cultural identity. This includes a strong emphasis on cultural preservation and adaptation, with the goal of achieving independence while upholding their unique social contract and tribal instincts. The recipients of these behaviors, including themselves, other cultures, and Australia, respond with a mix of adaptation and rejection. This cultural emphasis on preserving and adapting traditions is widely regarded as a significant aspect of the sampled population's beliefs and practices within Papua New Guinean society.

In Papua New Guinea, it is a common cultural practice for people to habitually chew betel nut, which is likened to the effects of speed and Crystal Meth and is associated with high rates of oral cancer. This habit is deeply ingrained in the culture and is widely regarded as a normative behavior by a significant portion of the sampled population. The cultural significance of betel nut chewing is evident in its widespread acceptance and prevalence within the community. Despite the health risks associated with this practice, it remains a deeply ingrained aspect of Papua New Guinean culture.

People tend to communicate directly on general topics, but they are culturally very sensitive and are easily shamed, so a more indirect style is common when it comes to sensitive issues. Most people will be offended if you walk by and greet without stopping for a chat. This communicates that you do not have time for them, do not care, etc. It is considered better to express a criticism through a colleague or friend, rather than face to face.

More than arms length of personal space is best, especially w ith men communicat ing with woman and vice versa. Men need to keep an arms length distance from wom en they do not know. Not doing this may communicate some inappropriate interest and the man could be ‘courted’ for doing so. As you get to know each other better this space can be reduced to less than arms space. In family circles people get very close to each other. f b usiness colleagues know each other well they may get close r when communicati ng, but normally they will remain at arms length. In PNG , people are not offended by appropriate touching. Men will often hold hands with each other even in public and this will not be strange. This will happen between strangers as well. For example you may ask directions, and the man will take your hand and walk with you. It’s a sure sign of friendship. People who know each other better will hug each other, touch shoulders and arms, and stroke each other’s calves. Once again this kind of touching will mainly happen between people who know each other better and men will not touch wom e n in this way. It may happen that older women (grandmothers ) may touch men, hug them, stroke their calves, etc.

Direct eye contact is appropriate in all situations. You will find that children are shy and therefore avoid eye contact but this tends to change as they become familiar with you. Avoiding eye contact will be seen as negative and communicates being sly.

Most people do not keep time and work according to the sun. They get up in the morning when it’s starts to get light, lunch at noon, visit when it’s dark and sleep at about 8PM. Usually nothing happens on time due to the fact that most people do not keep time. In general people are not offended if you are late, and you will need to be aware of the fact that people will come late or arrive early for appointments. Services like buses do not run on time, there is no time schedule. You can wait up to an hour or more for a bus. In general planes arrive on time but often they are late as well and sometimes will not arrive. People will usually offer their time freely; they love to serve and help and do not covet their time. This is a major sign of friendship and coveting your time will be s sure sign that you are not a friend. I n business circles , people tend to be more on time, and may even be offended if you are very late.

In most rural areas, women do not have any status. Their names are changed when they get married and they exist to serve the men and work in the gardens. In general, a woman’s role is generally taking care of the home, cooking, etc. Women cannot challenge men in public or participate in public debates or court cases. This is true of foreign woman as well. In more developed parts of the country, women have more rights but will still be looked down upon for the most part. Women usually cover their thighs and most women will wear dresses.

You call people to come to you by pointing your fingers downward and making a scratching motion. When moving though a crowd that sits on the ground or back of a truck (taxi) you can bend down low, point downwards with a flat hand and start walking, they will then open up. You will find that some people will point with their chin instead of a finger . It is not good to point to people that are not part of your conversation. They may be offended and think that you are gossiping.

Most people will be offended if you walk by and greet without stopping for a chat. This communicates that you do not have time for them, do not care, etc. To step over food is considered very rude . Homosexual activity is illegal.

Due to the extreme isolated location of many tribes, laws are difficult to enforce in much of the country. There is no legal drinking age. Penalties for possession or use of, or trafficking in illegal drugs are severe, and convicted offenders can expect long jail sentences and heavy fines. Homosexual activity is illegal.

The traditional Melanesian cultures (more than 200 have been identified) are kept alive in elaborate rituals involving deaths, feasts, marriages, compensation ceremonies and initiation rites. Visitors to country areas, especially in the highlands, will often find local variations in village construction, dialect and dress.
